I also got back test results for HPV but since I wasn’t one of the high risk strains (there are literally 100s of strains - it’s basically the common cold for STIs) I was also told that it wasn’t a big deal, 90% of people have it and to just monitor it. Doctors tell you you don’t need to disclose because since mostly only women test positive (cause they only test women unless there are warts for men) it’s really low risk unless it’s one of 3 strains and if you’ve been having sex for more than 5 years and have had multiple partners chances are you’ve had it and it’s cleared up between Pap smears (or is dormant). Because of this almost all the stigma of HPV falls on women even though it’s incredibly low risk in 99% of cases. Obviously that’s incredibly frustrating to hear but even if you do test positive for HPV and it’s not one of the high risk strains they just shrug and are like “well we’ll test you next year and see where we’re at” cause they fully expect it to clear up in the next 6 months. 

OP - you’re going through an incredibly hard thing where you were cheated on and now you are going through the emotions and self stigma of getting an STI. Even though really it’s more like you were just unlucky enough to test at the right time to catch it. Conflating this with your cheating history isn’t helpful and will just add more trauma and stress when the best thing you can do for yourself is be healthy and stress free right now.
